setupSteps: Warm up first. 2 to 5 minutes of walking on the spot, arm circles and a few easy hip circles. Do not do a deep triangle with cold hamstrings.
Floor. Flat, non-slip. A sticky mat or bare feet on a dry floor; never socks on tiles. Both feet must stay planted.
Wall. For the wall version, stand with the back of the pelvis and the back heel close to a smooth wall. Clear a space about 1 m wide.
Block. Keep a block (or a stack of books about 20 to 25 cm high, est.) beside the front foot, outside the foot, ready for the lower hand.
Clothing. Stretchy pants or shorts; a long kurta tucked or tied so you can see the legs; no tight jeans.
Mat direction. Face the long side of the room (or the long edge of the mat) so the legs spread along the mat.
Camera. Phone on a shelf at hip height, 2.5 to 3 m in front, so the whole body, both feet and the hands are in frame (see sections 11 and 12).

steps.title: Stand tall in Tadasana
steps.action: stand with the feet together, arms by the sides, weight even on both feet.
steps.visualCheck: front view, head over the hips, shoulders level.

steps.title: Step the feet wide
steps.action: step or walk the feet apart about 3 to 3.5 feet (about 90 to 105 cm, est.; roughly one long leg-length). A beginner can start slightly narrower.
steps.feel: a wide steady base, legs strong.
steps.visualCheck: front view, feet well apart, toes of both feet pointing forward toward the long side of the mat.

steps.title: Raise the arms (optional)
steps.action: lift the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, palms down, in line with the shoulders.
steps.visualCheck: front view, arms in one line from fingertip to fingertip.

steps.title: Turn the right foot out
steps.action: turn the right foot out 90 degrees so the toes point to the right short end of the mat. The right heel lines up with the middle of the left arch.
steps.feel: the right thigh turning out; no twist in the knee.
steps.visualCheck: right kneecap points the same way as the right toes.

steps.title: Turn the left foot in
steps.action: turn the left foot in about 15 to 30 degrees (sources range 15 to 45). Keep the left leg straight and the left foot flat.
steps.visualCheck: front view, left foot slightly angled in, not rolled onto its edge.

steps.title: Square the hips
steps.action: keep the hips facing forward toward the long side of the mat as much as comfortable; the pelvis opens a little to the right but is not forced.
steps.feel: both legs active; the front thigh turning out, not forced.
steps.visualCheck: front view, both hip points roughly level.

steps.title: Lengthen the spine
steps.action: breathe in and stretch up through the crown of the head, ribs lifted.
steps.visualCheck: the torso is not leaning yet.

steps.title: Hinge from the front hip
steps.action: breathe out, push the right hip back and send the torso out over the right leg, as if sliding the hip crease back; keep both sides of the waist long. Do not side-bend the spine.
steps.feel: a stretch in the back of the right thigh and the inner groin; both legs working.
steps.visualCheck: front view, the torso comes out over the leg in a long line with no collapse into the right side.

steps.title: Place the lower hand
steps.action: when you cannot go further with a long spine, rest the right hand on the shin, or on a block placed outside the right foot, or on the ankle. Never rest the hand on the knee joint.
steps.feel: support, not pressure; no pinch in the knee.
steps.visualCheck: hand on the shin below the knee or on the block; the knee is clear.

steps.title: Reach the top arm up
steps.action: stretch the left arm up so both arms form a line, the top arm over the shoulder. Options: arm straight up; top hand on the top hip (easiest); top arm reaching over the ear (harder).
steps.visualCheck: front view, arms in a line from the lower hand up through the top hand.

steps.title: Choose the gaze
steps.action: look at the top hand if the neck is comfortable; otherwise look straight ahead, or down at the floor or big toe.
steps.visualCheck: chin not jammed, neck not craned.

steps.title: Hold
steps.action: keep both knees straight but soft, and press the feet into the floor.
steps.feel: stretch in the thigh and side; mild, never pain.
steps.tempo: about 15 to 30 seconds (est.; 5 breaths is about 25 seconds).

steps.title: Come up
steps.action: breathe in, press the back foot down, lead with the chest and the top arm and rise with a long spine. Bring the arms down.
steps.feel: the legs working as you lift.
steps.visualCheck: no jerking up with the neck.

steps.title: Switch
steps.action: turn the feet to the other side and repeat. Do both sides each round.

commonMistakes.title: Side-bending instead of hinging
commonMistakes.text: Side-bending instead of hinging. The waist collapses on the lower side, the chest turns toward the floor. Fix: slide the front hip back and lengthen both sides of the waist; use a block.

commonMistakes.title: Hand on the knee
commonMistakes.text: Hand on the knee. Pressure on the knee joint can strain it; the front knee may hyperextend. Fix: hand on the shin, ankle or a block.

commonMistakes.title: Locked, hyperextended front knee
commonMistakes.text: Locked, hyperextended front knee. It can overstretch the back of the knee. Fix: keep a micro-bend, press the foot down, engage the thigh.

commonMistakes.title: Stance too wide
commonMistakes.text: Stance too wide. The pelvis tilts and the hamstrings overstretch (BODi trainer snippet prefers a shorter stance). Fix: shorten the stance until the hips stay level.

commonMistakes.title: Forcing the hand to the floor
commonMistakes.text: Forcing the hand to the floor. You lose the line and tense the neck. Fix: use a block, or the shin; the line matters more than touching.

commonMistakes.title: Cranking the neck up
commonMistakes.text: Cranking the neck up. Looking up while the chin is misaligned strains the neck. Fix: look ahead or down.

commonMistakes.title: Back foot too flat and back knee turned
commonMistakes.text: Back foot too flat and back knee turned. Twists the knee. Fix: turn the back foot in 15 to 30 degrees and keep the knees pointing the same way as the toes.

commonMistakes.title: Hips rolling forward and leaning forward
commonMistakes.text: Hips rolling forward and leaning forward. The pose becomes a forward fold. Fix: use the wall behind you.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath or hurrying out
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath or hurrying out. Dizziness, especially with high blood pressure. Fix: slow nose breaths; rise slowly.

safetyNotes: Mild tension, never pain. Stop at pain in the knee, back, neck or hamstring.

Neck: keep the neck neutral; if the neck is tender, look straight ahead or down and do not turn the head up (YogaUOnline, Art of Living, snippets). Cervical spondylitis was listed as a contraindication by one yoga institute.

Hamstring: do not force depth; a recent hamstring strain means skip or use the shortest hinge (a hamstring caution appears in a revolved-triangle source; standard triangle is generally described as a hamstring stretch).

Lower back: hinge from the hip, keep the spine long, use the wall and a block. Severe back problems: a yoga teacher or physio first (snippet). A slipped disc was on one institute's contraindication list.
Knee: hand on shin or block, never the knee; soft knee, no locking.
Blood pressure and dizziness: do not hold the breath; rise slowly; look down for high blood pressure (one guide); if you feel dizzy, sit down.
Stop immediately if you feel: sharp pain, numbness or tingling in the arm or leg, dizziness, chest pain or breathlessness, or a pull or pop in the hamstring.
Spotter: not needed; use a wall.
Gym etiquette: use a clear mat area and keep the block out of the walkway.

Stance width: about 3 to 4 feet, one leg's distance, or a shorter stance. We chose 3 to 3.5 feet, shorter for beginners.
Back-foot angle: 15, 30 to 45 and 45 degrees across sources. We chose 15 to 30 degrees for beginners.
Hand placement: shin, ankle, block or floor; the knee is advised against. We chose shin or block.
Gaze: up to the top hand (classic) versus ahead or down for neck or blood-pressure concerns. We offer all three, default ahead for beginners.
Lower-back pain: sources conflict (avoid versus helpful). We chose "modify" with wall and block.
